chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام:
About a lost item found by a poor person—whether he is regarding it in the same position as a wealthy person. So he said: “Yes.”
He said: “And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام used to say: ‘It belongs to its owners; do not touch it.’”

He said: And I asked him about a man who finds a dirham, a garment, or an animal—what should he do? He said: “He should announce it for one year. If it is not recognized, he should place it among his property until its claimant comes, then he gives it to him. And if he dies, he should make a bequest concerning it, and he is liable for it.”

key_terms.أَوْصَى بِهَا: he makes a bequest concerning it before death
key_terms.اللُّقَطَةِ: lost property that has been found
key_terms.الْغَنِيِّ: a wealthy person, mentioned for legal comparison
key_terms.الْفَقِيرُ: a poor person who finds the item
key_terms.دَابَّةً: a riding or transport animal that is found
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a coin or monetary unit found as lost property
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally responsible and liable for it
key_terms.يُعَرِّفُهَا: he publicizes and announces the found item

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in Shiʿi fiqh if he finds lost property such as money, clothing, or an animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on lost property, stating that the poor person is treated the same as the wealthy person with respect to found items. A found item remains the right of its owner, must be announced for a year, and the finder remains responsible for returning it whenever the owner appears.
